questions.q: Which two methods does every gymnasium.Env subclass implement to be usable by stable-baselines3?
options: connect() and disconnect()
sample() and score()
reset() and step()
train() and evaluate()
questions.explain: reset() starts a new episode and returns an observation; step() takes an action and returns the next observation, reward, and termination flags.

questions.q: What does QueryPlanEnv's reset() method actually do?
options: Trains the PPO policy for one step
Samples a fresh (date_range_days, territory) pair and returns an observation, without touching the database
Clears all previously logged logical-read statistics
Executes the hinted SQL query against the sandbox
questions.explain: reset() only samples the episode's parameters and builds the observation vector — no SQL executes until step() is called.

questions.q: How does the environment capture logical reads for a query?
options: By estimating them from the query's text length
By running SET STATISTICS IO ON and parsing the resulting messages on the pyodbc cursor
By calling a stable-baselines3 built-in cost estimator
By reading them from the SQL Server query plan XML only
questions.explain: SET STATISTICS IO ON makes SQL Server emit per-table read statistics as messages, which pyodbc exposes on the cursor and a small parser extracts.

questions.q: What do step()'s terminated and truncated flags get set to, and why?
options: terminated=False, truncated=True, because episodes never end
Both True, because every episode hits a time limit
terminated=True, truncated=False, because one query decision is the entire episode
Both False, because the environment loops forever
questions.explain: Every episode ends after exactly one step — there's no horizon to truncate, matching the contextual-bandit framing from Lesson 4.

questions.q: Why does the QueryPlanEnv constructor take a precomputed list of territories with their customer counts, rather than querying it fresh each episode?
options: stable-baselines3 requires all observations to be hardcoded
It makes the territory-size proxy in the observation cheap to compute at reset time
SQL Server does not allow repeated SELECT queries
Customer counts change every time a query runs
questions.explain: Precomputing the territory list avoids an extra database round-trip on every reset() call just to build part of the observation.
